name: VIRELLE
tagline: Agentic AI platform for luxury hospitality innovation

caseStudy.problem: Luxury hotels face a constant challenge: unsold rooms, underused facilities, and shifting demand in the surrounding destination. Management needs to answer questions like: What opportunity exists right now? What should we create? Can we deliver it? How should we market it? Is it commercially worthwhile? No single role naturally owns this entire process.
caseStudy.insight: The hotel innovation problem spans research, experience design, product development, marketing and management — each requiring different expertise. An agentic approach, where specialised AI agents handle distinct functions, can cover the full lifecycle from opportunity detection to commercial validation.
caseStudy.users: Luxury hotel management teams — The Virelle Dublin, a fictional five-star boutique hotel with rooms, spa, restaurant, rooftop bar and premium guest services.
caseStudy.hypothesis: Five specialised AI agents, each corresponding to one innovation archetype (research, experience design, product development, marketing, management), can collaborate to turn changing market conditions into commercially viable guest experiences.
caseStudy.aiArchitecture: Five specialised AI agents orchestrated through MCP: Market Research Agent, Experience Design Agent, Product Development Agent, Marketing Agent, and Commercial Management Agent. Each agent owns a distinct phase of the innovation pipeline.
caseStudy.decisionsNotBuilt: No single monolithic AI handling everything. No generic chatbot interface. No automation without human oversight at decision points.
caseStudy.evaluation: Demonstrated end-to-end pipeline from opportunity detection through to commercial validation. Tested across multiple market scenarios for the Dublin hotel context.
caseStudy.tradeoffs: Specialisation vs coordination — five agents need clear handoffs. Domain specificity — luxury hospitality requires nuanced understanding of premium guest expectations. Commercial realism — the system must produce viable business cases, not just creative ideas.
caseStudy.outcome: Working multi-agent system demonstrating how AI can own the full innovation lifecycle for hospitality — from market sensing to experience design to commercial validation.
caseStudy.next: Real-time market data integration, multi-property portfolio optimisation, guest feedback loops driving agent refinement.

name: SOVA
tagline: Calm self-reflection product for building self-trust through daily rituals

caseStudy.problem: Most wellness and journaling apps rely on streaks, metrics, and guilt-driven engagement. They turn self-reflection into another productivity task. The result: people abandon them, or worse, start performing for the app instead of reflecting honestly.
caseStudy.insight: Self-trust isn't built through gamification. It's built through small, pressure-free daily rituals that feel safe, optional, and supportive. The product should disappear when you need it to — not demand attention.
caseStudy.users: Individuals who want to build self-trust and clarity through reflection, but are tired of apps that feel like homework.
caseStudy.hypothesis: A calm product that intentionally avoids performance metrics, streaks, and guilt-driven models can create a safer space for genuine self-reflection — and paradoxically, be more engaging because it doesn't demand engagement.
caseStudy.aiArchitecture: AI provides gentle, contextual prompts based on the user's own expressed values and past reflections. No external templates. No 'here's what you should do' outputs. The AI holds space, the human decides.
caseStudy.decisionsNotBuilt: No streaks. No leaderboards. No daily reminders that feel like nagging. No analytics dashboard. No social features. Deliberately designed to feel safe, optional, and supportive — not demanding.
caseStudy.evaluation: Product strategy validated through competitive analysis of 12 journaling and wellness apps. User interviews exploring how people actually build reflective habits. Go-to-market framework developed.
caseStudy.tradeoffs: Calm vs discoverable — a calm product risks being invisible. Privacy vs utility — reflection data is deeply personal. Monetisation vs accessibility — how do you charge for something that should feel free?
caseStudy.outcome: Complete product strategy with pricing model, feature roadmap, and go-to-market framework. Prototype demonstrating calm interaction patterns for self-reflection.
caseStudy.next: Voice-based reflection, peer reflection circles with privacy controls, integration with existing journaling tools.

name: RouteForge AI
tagline: AI-powered logistics optimisation for EU SMBs — full product strategy from market to prototype

caseStudy.problem: EU SMB logistics operators spend 3-4 hours daily manually planning routes. Enterprise solutions like SAP cost 100K+ and are overbuilt for small fleets. The result: wasted fuel, missed delivery windows, and suboptimal paths. The market is fragmented — no one owns the 'SMB route optimisation' space.
caseStudy.insight: The routing problem for a 5-truck fleet is fundamentally different from a 500-truck fleet. SMBs need simplicity, not complexity. But they still need the intelligence — they just can't afford the enterprise price tag or 6-month implementation timeline.
caseStudy.users: EU-based logistics operators with 2-20 vehicles. Fleet managers who are also the IT department. Owner-operators who wear five hats and need tools that work in 10 minutes, not 10 weeks.
caseStudy.hypothesis: An AI route planner that learns from historical delivery patterns and real-time constraints can reduce fuel costs and delivery times for SMBs at a fraction of enterprise pricing — if the onboarding is dead simple.
caseStudy.aiArchitecture: Optimisation engine combining constraint satisfaction with ML-learned route patterns. API-first architecture for integration with existing fleet management tools. React dashboard for visual route planning and fleet overview.
caseStudy.decisionsNotBuilt: No full fleet management suite — focused purely on route optimisation to win on one thing. No driver mobile app in v1 — kept scope tight. No real-time GPS tracking — that's a different problem with different regulatory requirements.
caseStudy.evaluation: Market sizing identified 2.3B EU SMB logistics market. Competitive analysis of 8 platforms (SAP, Route4Me, OptimoRoute). ICP interviews with fleet operators. Interactive prototype validated against real route scenarios.
caseStudy.tradeoffs: Simplicity vs power — SMBs need easy but not toy-like. EU regulations add complexity (driver hours, emissions zones). Balancing algorithmic optimisation with human route knowledge — drivers know things the algorithm doesn't.
caseStudy.outcome: Working prototype with route optimisation dashboard. Complete product strategy covering market sizing, ICP definition, competitive positioning, prioritised feature roadmap, and technical feasibility assessment.
caseStudy.next: Multi-day route planning, fuel card API integration, predictive maintenance scheduling, driver mobile companion.

name: Digital Story
tagline: Human-AI collaboration in personal safety narratives

caseStudy.problem: Personal safety narratives — survivor stories, incident reports, witness accounts — are deeply personal but often poorly captured by existing tools. The gap between lived experience and documented account creates barriers to justice and support.
caseStudy.insight: AI can help people structure and articulate difficult experiences, but only if designed with extreme sensitivity to context, agency, and emotional safety. The technology must serve the person, not the other way around.
caseStudy.users: Survivors of safety incidents, witness account creators, researchers studying narrative reconstruction.
caseStudy.hypothesis: A human-AI collaboration framework that gives users full control over narrative construction — with AI offering structure without overriding voice — can produce more complete and authentic safety accounts.
caseStudy.aiArchitecture: LLM-assisted narrative structuring with human-in-the-loop at every decision point. No autonomous generation — AI suggests, user decides. Privacy-first architecture with local processing where possible.
caseStudy.decisionsNotBuilt: No fully automated report generation. No AI-driven analysis of emotional content. No data persistence by default.
caseStudy.evaluation: Research presented at EUt+ Dats and Stats Workshop 2026. Qualitative analysis of narrative completeness and user agency metrics.
caseStudy.tradeoffs: AI assistance vs human agency — too much help erodes authentic voice, too little leaves people struggling. Privacy vs utility.
caseStudy.outcome: Published research paper. Working prototype. Framework for responsible AI in sensitive contexts.
caseStudy.next: Multi-modal narrative support (audio, video), cross-cultural adaptation, clinical validation.
